subject: MicroBurst private offer — rev-share & payment term harmonization
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@microburst.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Private Offer (AWS) — rev-share ask + payment terms

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. MicroBurst is ready to move forward if we can get a private offer on AWS that meets two key commercial asks: a 45% marketplace rev-share for the first 12 months and Net60 payment terms. Our expected committed monthly spend is ~$210k for the first year (mostly real-time inference for 24/7 retail workloads).

We previously saw Redwood’s standard marketplace split at 30% and Net30 billing — the 45% / Net60 combination is a must for finance approval on our side given channel economics and cashflow. We also requested a SOC2 snapshot and the SOW; attaching our internal PO template for reference.

Can you route this to deal desk / execs for review? We’re targeting a signed PO by end of month (Deal ID MB-2027-0891).

Thanks,
Sara Kim
Head of Procurement | MicroBurst Retail
procurement@microburst.com
Attachments: MicroBurst_PO_Template.docx

Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Private Offer (AWS) — rev-share ask + payment terms

Hi Sara — thank you, and great to hear you’re ready to proceed. I’ll escalate internally to get a private-offer assessment and exec sign-off.

Quick notes for transparency:
- Deal ID: MB-2027-0891
- Customer ask: 45% rev-share (12m), Net60 billing

I’ve attached the MicroBurst SOW and our draft private offer for review (internal). Will loop in Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal to confirm whether we can accommodate Net60 and the requested split. Expect an internal reply by EOD tomorrow.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: MicroBurst private offer — ask for exec alignment (MB-2027-0891)

Folks — forwarding customer request. TL;DR: MicroBurst wants 45% rev-share on AWS private offer for 12 months + Net60. They’re committing ~210k/mo initially, profile looks steady with seasonal spikes.

Business impact / risks:
- Revenue math: 45% marketplace rev-share materially reduces Redwood take on this workload. With expected utilization the first year, incremental absolute revenue to Redwood from hosted ops would be ~1.4M gross; but margin and CAC for marketplace listings must be considered.
- Cashflow: Net60 increases DSO for marketplace settlement; we have to check if finance can accept this without escrow or advanced billing.
- Precedent: Approving 45% sets a new high-water mark for private offer splits for retailers; could create future expectations.

Options I see:
1) Decline rev-share and offer standard 30% / Net30 — risk losing the deal.
2) Approve temporary concession: 35% rev-share for first 12 months then revert to 30% thereafter; require Net45 and a 6mo performance/usage review.
3) Approve customer ask (45% / Net60) only with a platform fee/top-up (e.g., 10% fixed platform fee on consumption) or an upfront commit/retainer to cover DSO risk.

Requested: need an exec decision on which path to take (option 2 preferred by Deal Desk). Legal to confirm contract language and Finance to sign off on Net45 vs Net60. Jordan, please confirm whether MicroBurst can accept Net45 and a 6mo review window.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Deal Desk Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MicroBurst private offer — ask for exec alignment (MB-2027-0891)

Karthik — good summary. I prefer option 2 with concrete guardrails. My conditional approval:
- Split: 35% rev-share for the first 12 months, then 30% thereafter.
- Payment terms: Net45 (compromise).
- Requirement: Customer signs a 12-month commitment and we include a performance review at month 6 with metrics (avg monthly spend, token-level error rates, SLO adherence).
- Finance: need an escrow or a 2-week pre-bill in month 1 to mitigate DSO exposure; Laura please confirm feasibility.

We should also add a carve-out that this concession is one-off and not precedent. Jordan, if MicroBurst rejects Net45 we should be prepared to walk away.

Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic GTM | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: MicroBurst private offer approval (MB-2027-0891) — executive sign-off

Team — after reviewing the math and customer urgency, I approve Marissa’s suggested path with one adjustment to improve cash protection:
- Commercial: 35% rev-share for months 1–12; 30% thereafter.
- Payment: Net45 billing.
- Cash protection: Require a one-month prepayment (applied as credit) at contract signature or a short escrow arrangement that covers 45 days of projected spend.
- Legal: include a non-precedent clause and a 6-month operational review (metrics defined by Jordan and CS).

Jordan — you have executive approval to present this to MicroBurst. If they accept these terms, get DocuSign prepared and coordinate with AWS Private Offers team to list under the agreed split. Please copy finance on the DocuSign envelope.

Approved by: Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Attachments: soc2_snapshot.pdf
